intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square and Medina Souks
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the sensory overload of Marrakech's iconic main square, filled with snake charmers, storytellers, and street food stalls. Wander through the labyrinthine souks to haggle for spices, leather goods, and handcrafted lanterns. A quintessential cultural experience that captures the soul of Morocco.

experiences.name: Overnight Sahara Desert Camel Trek and Bivouac Camp
experiences.description: Ride camels at sunset into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga. Spend the night in a traditional Berber bivouac camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake up for a spectacular desert sunrise. The ultimate Moroccan adventure experience.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Visit the Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellij tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then explore the Saadian Tombs, a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, offering a rare glimpse into the Saadian dynasty's grandeur.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a board and carve down the towering orange dunes of the Sahara for an adrenaline-pumping desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction, and the activity can be combined with quad biking across the desert landscape. A thrilling way to experience the vast, otherworldly terrain of the Moroccan Sahara.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class and Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a local chef for an authentic hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to select fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and saffron, then learn to prepare classic dishes such as lamb tagine, bastilla, and harira soup. End with a communal feast of your own creations.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take a budget-friendly petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50–70 MAD) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the nearby medina streets to get your bearings. Peek into local souks and absorb the sights and sounds of Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square (the famous main square) as dusk falls – watch snake charmers, acrobats, and storytellers for free. Browse the open-air food stalls on the square for a lively and affordable dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick and cheap street food near the medina – try a harira soup and msemen flatbread from a local stall (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna night market food stalls – grilled merguez sausages, kefta skewers, and fresh orange juice (~50–70 MAD total)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros or dollars to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport or a medina exchange bureau for better rates. Avoid unlicensed taxis. Keep your belongings secure in the busy square.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior and gardens are free and open to all). Then walk to the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and beautiful courtyards. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ancient Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Walk through the bustling souks of the medina – visit the dyers' souk, spice market, and leather goods lanes. Practice bargaining for small souvenirs. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate tilework and carved plaster.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for sunset views from a rooftop café terrace (order a mint tea ~15 MAD to secure your seat). Watch the square transform into a carnival of performers and food vendors below.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the riad – café au lait, msemen with honey and amlou (almond-argan paste), (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the medina – try a tagine (lamb or vegetable) with bread (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna – harira soup, snail broth (optional!), and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~40–60 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the medina has uneven cobblestones. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees) is respectful near religious sites. Hiring a guide for the souks is optional but unofficial guides can be pushy – politely decline if not needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring intricate mosaics and carved marble. Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a vast ruined 16th-century palace with sweeping views from the ramparts and resident storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD including the Berber Museum) – the iconic cobalt-blue garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Stroll through exotic plants and vibrant architecture. Afterward, explore the trendy Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood for a change of scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free traditional Gnawa music performance often found in Djemaa el-Fna or nearby cultural spaces in the evening. Explore the Mouassine neighborhood's atmospheric lamp-lit lanes.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, olive oil, and cheese from a local bakery/épicerie (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Budget restaurant near Majorelle – a simple Moroccan salad plate and couscous (~60–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant away from tourist areas for authentic and cheaper pricing – try pastilla (savory-sweet pigeon pie) or kefta tagine (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is the priciest attraction of the trip but worth it. Go early afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The Berber Museum inside is included in the ticket and is excellent for cultural context.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 07:00) on a shared budget minibus/CTM bus or a pre-booked budget group tour toward Merzouga and the Sahara Desert via the scenic Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge route. This is a long travel day (~9–10 hours with stops). Enjoy dramatic Atlas Mountain scenery, Berber villages, and kasbahs along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') – a brief stop to admire the Taourirt Kasbah from the outside (entry optional ~20 MAD). Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the dramatic Dadès Gorge with its winding road and towering rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga at dusk. Mount camels for a sunset camel trek (~1 hour, included in most budget desert camp packages) into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Watch the sun melt into the golden dunes. Arrive at your budget desert camp for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – bread, jam, coffee (~20–30 MAD or included in accommodation)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a simple local café in a small town along the route (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp (usually included in camp package) – tagine, salads, mint tea, and optional live Gnawa drumming around a campfire

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared group desert tour in advance from Marrakech for the best budget rates (~600–900 MAD per person including transport, camel trek, and desert camp overnight). Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Carry enough water for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot for a breathtaking sunrise over the Sahara – one of Morocco's most spectacular free experiences. Take photos, feel the silence of the desert, and watch the shifting colors of the dunes. Return to camp for breakfast. Optionally, rent a sandboard at the camp (~30–50 MAD) for dune surfing fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Merzouga village on foot or by bicycle (rentals ~50 MAD/hour). Visit the small Gnawa community near the lake (Dayet Srji) – a seasonal lake that attracts flamingos in spring. Walk to the edge of the dunes for more photography. Rest and relax at the camp or a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Second sunset over the dunes – either from the camp or with a short walk into the dunes. Enjoy another evening of Berber music, stargazing (March skies are excellent with minimal light pollution), and campfire storytelling with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at desert camp (usually included) – Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea
meals.lunch: Simple lunch at a local Merzouga café or village restaurant – tagine or omelette with bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner (included in package) or local auberge – Berber couscous with seven vegetables (~60–80 MAD if not included)

day_by_day.notes: Protect your camera and phone from fine sand using a zip-lock bag. Sunrise trek is the highlight of the entire trip – do not miss it. Reapply sunscreen frequently as desert sun is intense even in March. Stay hydrated.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – 2027-03-20 (Return Journey: Sahara to Marrakech via Todra Gorge)
day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga early morning (07:00) on the return shared transport to Marrakech. Stop at the spectacular Todra Gorge – towering 300-meter-high rose-colored canyon walls with a stream running through the base. Take a short 30-minute walk through the gorge (free). Interact with local Berber women selling handicrafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey back through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~20 MAD entry) – an ancient fortified ksar (village) that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the atmospheric mud-brick towers and ramparts with panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (around 19:00–20:00). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and enjoy a final relaxed evening walk through the medina for any last-minute souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at desert camp or packed snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Todra Gorge or Tinerhir – simple local tagine or sandwiches (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech – treat yourself to a slightly nicer sit-down local restaurant in the medina for a farewell Moroccan feast (~80–100 MAD) – try a mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) if available

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is a must-stop – allocate at least 1–1.5 hours here. The route back offers some of Morocco's most dramatic mountain scenery. Keep snacks and water in your bag for the long drive. Confirm return drop-off point with your tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Marrakech. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace – excellent collection of Moroccan art, ceramics, and textiles. Then explore the Mouassine Fountain area and the historic Chrob ou Chouf Fountain (free) with its exquisite carved cedar canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last souvenir shopping in the souks – pick up argan oil, spices, leather goods, or hand-painted ceramics. Head to the Mellah market for the best prices on spices and dried fruits. Visit the Cyber Parc Arsat Moulay Abdessalam (free public garden) for a peaceful final afternoon stroll under palm and orange trees.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset at a rooftop terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Arrange a petit taxi or airport transfer for your onward journey (negotiate in advance, ~50–70 MAD to airport).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café – traditional Moroccan breakfast spread with baghrir (semolina pancakes) and honey (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Last medina lunch – a bowl of harira soup, a briouate (fried pastry filled with cheese or meat), and fresh orange juice (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Early dinner before heading to airport – classic chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives at a budget medina restaurant (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for the taxi ride and airport check-in. Keep a small amount of MAD for last-minute purchases and tips. Tipping is customary in Morocco – 10–20 MAD for porters, guides, and camp staff is appreciated. Carry any argan oil or liquid products in checked luggage to avoid airport confiscation.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Take time to freshen up, unpack, and orient yourself with the property and surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory stroll through the nearby Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) district — Marrakech's modern quarter. Browse the tree-lined Avenue Mohammed V, pop into a local patisserie, and get a feel for the city's rhythm without overwhelming yourself on arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to witness the nightly spectacle: snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls lighting up as the sun sets. Explore the edges of the medina and soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or at the airport upon arrival — skip or grab a light snack at a café in Gueliz such as Café du Livre.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a local café in Gueliz — try a croque monsieur or Moroccan harira soup and bread at a mid-range café (budget ~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the open-air food stalls in Djemaa el-Fna — try grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Authentic, affordable, and unforgettable (~60–100 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00 — Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for travel fatigue and settling in. Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in Gueliz. Keep your first evening relaxed and exploratory.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Marrakech's historic medina. Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (built in the 19th century), then walk to the nearby Saadian Tombs — a beautifully decorated royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Hire a local licensed guide from the palace entrance for context (~150–200 MAD for 2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ben Youssef Medersa, one of North Africa's largest and most ornate Quranic schools, with its intricate zellige tilework and carved cedarwood. Afterwards, get gloriously lost in the souks — navigate the labyrinthine lanes of the medina browsing spices, leather goods, lanterns, and textiles in the Souk Semmarine area.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan cooking class or visit the Maison de la Photographie rooftop for panoramic medina views at golden hour. End the evening with a mint tea ceremony at a rooftop riad café overlooking the medina skyline.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — Moroccan breakfast of msemen flatbread, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, and café au lait (~50–80 MAD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices in the Place Rahba Kedima — a beloved mid-range spot with tagines, salads, and great medina views (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant — try Le Foundouk near the Ben Youssef Medersa for lamb tagine with prunes and almonds in a beautifully restored setting (~180–250 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina streets are uneven cobblestones. Bargaining in the souks is expected and part of the experience; start at roughly 40–50% of the asking price. Keep small change handy for tips.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley in the High Atlas Mountains (~30 km from Marrakech). Hire a shared grand taxi or join a small group tour. Trek through Berber villages, terraced fields, and along the Ourika River. Visit a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women to learn about traditional production.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Setti Fatma waterfalls — a series of seven cascades reachable by a short but rewarding hike. Swim in the natural pools if weather permits (March can be cool but refreshing). Explore the small weekly Berber market if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech in the late afternoon. Unwind with a hammam experience — visit a mid-range traditional hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or a local neighbourhood hammam for a full scrub and steam ritual (~150–250 MAD for a tourist-friendly package).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — Moroccan pastries, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — fresh trout from the river, Moroccan salads, and khobz bread with a stunning mountain backdrop (~100–140 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Marrakech at a local neighbourhood restaurant in the medina — try pastilla (a flaky pigeon or chicken pie with almonds and cinnamon) at a family-run spot (~120–180 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ourika Valley transport the evening before — a shared grand taxi costs approximately 20–30 MAD per person each way, or a private taxi ~200–300 MAD round trip. March weather in the Atlas can be chilly — bring a light layer. Hammam visit is best booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (around 07:00) for the Sahara Desert via a shared group transfer or private driver through the Draa Valley. The journey (~9–10 hours total) passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m), the ancient kasbah town of Aït Benhaddou (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and the rose-red city of Ouarzazate. Stop at Aït Benhaddou for a guided walk through the fortified ksar (~1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley — a lush palm-lined river oasis cutting through the desert — passing through Agdz and Zagora. The landscape shifts dramatically from mountains to hammada (rocky desert) to palm groves. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi area by late afternoon or early evening (depending on exact route chosen).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp near the Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount dromedary camels for a 45-minute sunset camel trek into the dunes — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Watch the sun melt into the Sahara horizon from the top of a golden dune.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before 07:00 departure — pack a snack for the road.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in Ouarzazate at a mid-range restaurant — try a chicken tagine with olives and preserved lemon (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — a communal meal of harira soup, tagine, Moroccan salads, and fresh fruit under a sky blazing with stars (~included in most camp packages or ~150–200 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~9–10 hours driving). Book your transport and desert camp well in advance — mid-range desert camps with private tents, en-suite facilities, and electricity cost approximately 600–1,200 MAD per night. The Marrakech–Merzouga route is best done as a 2-night minimum in the desert. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a warm layer for the cold desert night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) and climb the nearest dune crest to watch the Sahara dawn — the light turns the dunes from deep orange to gold to pale cream in minutes. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast. Spend the morning sandboarding down the dunes, exploring the erg on foot, or visiting the nearby village of Merzouga to interact with local Amazigh (Berber) families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gnawa musicians' village near Khamlia — a small community known for their hypnotic spiritual music rooted in sub-Saharan African traditions. Attend an informal performance. Alternatively, rent a 4x4 for a guided desert excursion to fossil sites, nomad encampments, and hidden oases in the surrounding hammada.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the dune camp for the second sunset. Gather around the campfire for traditional Gnawa music performed by camp musicians. Stargaze in the Sahara's near-zero light-pollution sky — on a clear March night, the Milky Way is visible with the naked eye.

meals.breakfast: Berber camp breakfast — khobz bread, olive oil, honey, amlou, Moroccan mint tea, and soft-boiled eggs.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp or in Merzouga village — harira, Moroccan salad, and fresh dates.
meals.dinner: Second night camp dinner — communal Berber feast with tagine, couscous, and traditional sweets around the campfire.

day_by_day.notes: March nights in the Sahara can drop to 5–10°C — bring a warm jacket and socks. Camel trekking and sandboarding are typically included in mid-range camp packages. Tipping your camel guide (~50 MAD) and camp staff (~100 MAD) is customary and appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: After a final sunrise at the dunes, depart the desert camp and begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different, equally scenic southern route: through Rissani (historic gateway to the Sahara and birthplace of the Alaouite dynasty), Erfoud (famous for fossil marble), and the Ziz Valley — a breathtaking gorge lined with tens of thousands of date palms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Midelt for a late lunch break in the Middle Atlas mountains. Continue through the cedar forests of Azrou (home to wild Barbary macaque monkeys — a delightful roadside stop). Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Check back into your accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — revisit Djemaa el-Fna one last time with fresh eyes and new appreciation. Browse for last-minute souvenirs in the evening souks. Treat yourself to a nicer dinner to celebrate the journey.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Midelt — a mountain town known for its apple orchards. Try a hearty lamb or vegetable tagine at a local restaurant (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a well-regarded mid-range Marrakech restaurant — try Nomad in the medina for modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views (lamb mechoui, spiced carrot salad, bastilla dessert) (~200–280 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: The return route via Rissani and Ziz Valley adds approximately 1–2 hours to the journey but is highly recommended for its distinct landscape. Stop briefly at Erfoud's fossil workshops to see craftsmen cutting and polishing 400-million-year-old marine fossils from the local black marble — a fascinating and free experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden, a stunning 12-acre botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. The cobalt-blue Villa Majorelle houses the Berber Museum with an exceptional collection of Amazigh jewelry, textiles, and artifacts (~70 MAD entry). Arrive early (09:00) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and the ornate El Bahia Palace gardens one last time. Visit the Museum of Marrakech in the beautifully restored 19th-century Mnebhi Palace for a final dose of Moroccan art and architecture. Do any remaining souvenir shopping — argan oil, saffron, Moroccan leather slippers (babouches), and hand-painted ceramics make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Early evening transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure, or if your flight is the following day, enjoy a final relaxed sunset mint tea on a medina rooftop, reflecting on seven extraordinary days across one of the world's most captivating countries.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — indulge in a full Moroccan spread with beghrir (semolina pancakes), honey, and argan oil.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Majorelle Garden — try Grand Café de la Poste in Gueliz, a colonial-era brasserie serving Moroccan-French fusion cuisine (~130–180 MAD).
meals.dinner: Light pre-departure dinner or airport meal — or if staying, a final tagine at a trusted medina favourite discovered during the week (~100–150 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is closed on certain religious holidays — check the calendar in advance. Book entry tickets online to avoid queues. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Marrakech Menara. Keep approximately 200–300 MAD in cash for final tips, porter fees, and small purchases. Carry any argan oil in checked luggage (liquids restriction).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort with a personal concierge greeting and chilled welcome beverages en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a private welcome ritual with traditional Moroccan mint tea and dates. Take a leisurely stroll through the resort gardens to decompress from travel. Optional: indulge in a 60-minute hammam and argan oil massage at the resort spa to refresh after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Private guided evening walk through the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square — witness the transformation as snake charmers, storytellers, and food vendors ignite the plaza at dusk. Return for an intimate rooftop dinner at the resort with panoramic views of the Atlas Mountains silhouetted against the sunset sky.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (arrival day)
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze platter and freshly squeezed juices served in your suite upon check-in
meals.dinner: Private rooftop dinner at the resort featuring a curated Moroccan tasting menu — bastilla au pigeon, slow-braised lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and a saffron crème brûlée, paired with Moroccan rosé from the Meknes region

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport and travel documents are readily accessible for check-in. Request the resort butler to pre-arrange a wake-up call and confirm Day 2 experiences. The hammam should be booked in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Medina of Marrakech. Begin at the magnificent Koutoubia Mosque (exterior), then wind through the historic souks — spice markets, leather tanneries, and artisan workshops. Visit the opulent Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings. Accompanied by an expert cultural historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive visit to the Saadian Tombs, discovered in 1917 and dating to the 16th century. Continue to the El Badi Palace ruins for a sweeping overview of Marrakech's imperial grandeur. Afterward, a private shopping experience in the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) with a personal stylist to curate authentic Moroccan textiles, jewelry, and leather goods with no haggling pressure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a prestigious riad rooftop bar in the Medina. Followed by a private dinner at one of Marrakech's most celebrated restaurants — a riad setting with live Gnawa music, traditional Moroccan courses served in ceremonial fashion.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast spread at the resort — msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh fruit platters, harira soup, and Berber coffee
meals.lunch: Exclusive lunch at a hidden riad restaurant in the Medina — chicken bastilla pastilla, zaalouk eggplant salad, and fresh-squeezed orange with orange blossom water
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-tier Marrakech riad restaurant (e.g., Dar Yacout or similar luxury establishment) — seven-course traditional Moroccan feast with live entertainment

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina tour — cobblestone streets can be uneven. The private guide will navigate the labyrinthine alleys seamlessly. Dress modestly near religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Marrakech palm groves and the Haouz Plain, with the Atlas Mountains as a dramatic backdrop. The approximately 1-hour flight is followed by a traditional Berber champagne breakfast in the countryside — a truly magical luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the extraordinary Majorelle Garden, the iconic cobalt-blue botanical sanctuary created by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the adjacent Berber Museum and the YSL Museum for a fascinating intersection of Moroccan heritage and haute couture. Enjoy a private curator-led tour.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive cooking class with a renowned Marrakchi chef in a luxury riad kitchen — learn to prepare traditional Moroccan dishes including tagine, couscous, and pastilla. The class culminates in a candlelit dinner of your own creations on a private terrace.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber breakfast in the countryside following the hot air balloon landing — fresh bread, honey, argan oil, olives, and Moroccan tea
meals.lunch: Light garden lunch at the Majorelle Garden café — mezze plates, Moroccan salads, and fresh citrus drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner of dishes prepared during your private cooking class, served in an intimate riad setting with Moroccan lantern ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights are weather-dependent — the operator will confirm the morning of. Bring a light layer as mornings can be cool at altitude in March. Book the Majorelle Garden in advance as it is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at a Berber village for a traditional tea ceremony and insight into mountain life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the stunning Draa Valley — a ribbon of lush palm groves and ancient kasbahs cutting through the arid landscape. Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou, a breathtaking fortified ksar (village) that has served as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour of the ancient mud-brick citadel.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your luxury desert camp near Merzouga or Zagora as the sun begins to descend. Mount purebred Arabian or Berber camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes. Arrive at a premium glamping camp — private Berber tent with en-suite facilities, plush furnishings, and electricity.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure — eggs prepared to order, pastries, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a heritage kasbah restaurant in Ouarzazate — lamb couscous, Berber omelette, and fresh dates
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast under the stars at the luxury desert camp — slow-cooked tagine, grilled meats, and Moroccan pastries, accompanied by live Gnawa drumming and music around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: The drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops — an early departure from Marrakech (around 07:00) is recommended. Pack a daypack with essentials for the desert camp as luggage will be transported separately. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private guided sunrise hike to the crest of the tallest Erg Chebbi dune — a transcendent experience as the Sahara ignites in shades of amber, rose, and gold. Optional: sandboarding down the dunes for an adrenaline rush. Return to camp for a peaceful breakfast as the desert comes to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the desert surroundings with a 4x4 dune bashing excursion led by an experienced Berber driver — traverse towering dune corridors and remote oasis areas. Visit a nomadic Berber family encampment for an authentic cultural exchange and traditional tea. Relax at the luxury camp in the afternoon — optional spa treatments available in-tent.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing experience with a professional astronomer and high-powered telescope — the Sahara offers some of the clearest, darkest skies on Earth. Constellations, planets, and the Milky Way are visible in extraordinary detail. Conclude with a private nightcap of Moroccan whisky (mint tea) and dates by the dying embers of the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the dune crest — thermos of Berber coffee, fresh bread, honey, and dates carried by your guide
meals.lunch: Leisurely camp lunch — Moroccan salads, grilled chicken, flatbreads, and fresh fruit served in the shade of a Berber canopy
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner in the open desert — a curated four-course menu with lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, and saffron-infused desserts

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), sunglasses, and a hat for daytime desert activities — UV intensity is high even in March. Closed-toe shoes are recommended for dune climbing. The stargazing session typically begins around 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise camel ride back through the dunes to the camp edge. Depart the desert by private luxury vehicle, heading back toward Marrakech via the scenic Ziz Valley and Tafilalt oasis — a lush date palm paradise stretching for miles. Stop at the ancient Sijilmassa ruins, once a great trans-Saharan trade city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the rose-filled valley of Kelaat M'Gouna (Rose Valley) — famous for its Damask rose fields, best appreciated in March before peak bloom. Visit a traditional rose water distillery and artisan cooperative. Continue through the Dades Gorge for spectacular canyon scenery — optional short hike to viewpoints above the gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury kasbah hotel in the Dades or Todra region for overnight. Enjoy a private terrace dinner overlooking the illuminated canyon walls as the stars emerge over the Atlas plateau.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast — Berber omelette, msemen, fresh juice, and mint tea before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a family-run kasbah restaurant in the Ziz Valley — harira soup, mixed Moroccan salads, and lamb tagine with prunes and almonds
meals.dinner: Private dinner on the kasbah terrace — four-course Moroccan menu featuring local specialties and a selection of Moroccan wines

day_by_day.notes: The return journey allows for a more relaxed pace with scenic stops. Confirm the luxury kasbah booking in advance as properties in the Dades region have limited premium availability. Rose Valley distillery visits may require advance arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a late breakfast and a rejuvenating hammam and massage treatment at the kasbah spa. Private transfer departs for Marrakech with a scenic stop at the Ourika Valley or the Agafay Desert (a lunar stone desert just 40 minutes from Marrakech) for a final dramatic landscape experience and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Marrakech and the Aegean Bliss Resort. Final afternoon at leisure — optional last-minute souvenir shopping in the Medina with a private guide, or simply relax by the resort pool with a cold glass of fresh orange juice. Optional: visit the Museum of Moroccan Arts and Crafts (Dar Si Said) for a curated finale of Moroccan heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a bespoke tasting menu designed by the executive chef celebrating the flavors of the entire journey, from Marrakech spice markets to Saharan campfires. Toast to an extraordinary week with a glass of premium Moroccan sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast at the kasbah — fresh pastries, eggs, fruit, Berber coffee, and orange blossom honey
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Agafay Desert or en route — mezze spread at a scenic desert lodge with Atlas Mountain views
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — seven courses celebrating Moroccan culinary heritage, paired with curated Moroccan and international wines

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with the resort concierge — if flying out on March 22, ensure a private airport transfer is pre-booked. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Pack any fragile souvenirs (ceramics, glassware) carefully using provided resort packaging materials. Tipping your guides and drivers at the end of the trip is customary and greatly appreciated.
